chapter: The Owls and New Orleans after the war
title: The Owls' fast tempos and head arrangements
summary: The Owls were hard to dance to because of fast tempos but wonderful to listen to, using mostly head arrangements. Souchon thinks Red Long played with them.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: we'd be happy with that No I think you could get more you know more about your audience than I do anyhow and you could ask him leading questions that would be very successful Now as I said that the owls they to me forsook the dance music that we were accustomed to dancing to and when they began being popular for the dances around New Orleans it was hard to dance to them their tempos were too fast and they had forsaken that easy going way you know but a very wonderful listening stuff and although they used music it was a bare outline their arrangements were intros and ride outs and maybe little duet breaks and things like that which were head arrangements and some of it was written arrangements but most of the time was all extemporaneous I think that Red Long I'm pretty sure he played with them for a while do you remember if I'm right on that trumpet
